title: Engineering Reasoning and Instruction (ERI) Benchmark: A Large Taxonomy-driven Dataset for Foundation Models and Agents
notes: engineering_arxiv: must-cite - the largest multi-branch engineering reasoning benchmark found (57,750 records over nine fields that include all five EngTrace branches, three difficulty tiers), scored on a five-point scale with multi-judge averaging and a cross-provider 'convergent validation' against judge circularity, so it is the direct foil for EngTrace's generated instances, gold traces, deterministic checks and out-of-roster judge.

title: Do VLMs Reason Like Engineers? A Benchmark and a Stage-wise Evaluation
notes: engineering_arxiv: must-cite - EngVQA (696 multimodal problems, five engineering subjects) argues, as EngTrace does, that final-answer scoring hides reasoning failures and scores eight solution stages separately with an automatic evaluator validated against human grades (Pearson 0.975); it is the closest stage-level engineering evaluation and must be contrasted with EngTrace's text-only generated instances and code-derived gold traces.

title: Power Systems Agent Benchmark: Executable Evaluation of AI Agents in Electric Power Engineering
notes: engineering_arxiv: must-cite - a power-engineering benchmark (41 task families, eight areas) whose deterministic evaluator recomputes the engineering quantities and whose held-out instances are synthesized by per-family generators from private seeds, the same contamination-resistance design as EngTrace's private-seed templates, applied to agent outputs rather than reasoning traces.

title: TPS-CalcBench: A Benchmark and Diagnostic Evaluation Framework for LLM Analytical Calculation Competence in Hypersonic Thermal Protection System Engineering
authors: Jinglai Zheng, Chuhan Qiao, Haiming Huang
notes: engineering_arxiv: must-cite - an engineering calculation benchmark (420 core items in hypersonic thermal-protection design) that scores result accuracy and reasoning quality on separate tracks, using an 8-dimension rubric and a calibrated judge with human audit to catch right-answer-wrong-reasoning, the failure EngTrace targets with milestone and arithmetic checks rather than a rubric judge.

title: From Answers to States: Verifiable Process-Level Evaluation of Chemical Reasoning in Large Language Models
notes: engineering_arxiv: must-cite - outside engineering (chemistry) but the closest verification design found: models must expose intermediate steps that deterministic rule verifiers and reference traces check instead of an LLM judge, with final-answer, template-adherence and step-verifier scores reported separately, which parallels EngTrace's answer check, milestone coverage and arithmetic check.

title: Sci-Rho: A Multilingual Visually-Grounded Symbolic Benchmark for STEM Problems
notes: engineering_arxiv: must-cite - outside engineering (visual STEM, seven languages) but built like EngTrace: 4,242 expert-written Python templates generate 42,420 instances paired with reasoning steps and ground truth, scored by worst-case accuracy across variants and step-level F1; Semantic Scholar lists it as citing EngTrace's arXiv version, so reviewers are likely to expect the comparison.

title: ThermoQA: A Three-Tier Benchmark for Evaluating Thermodynamic Reasoning in Large Language Models
notes: engineering_arxiv: must-cite - a thermodynamics benchmark (293 open-ended problems, three tiers) whose ground truth, including intermediate states, is computed with CoolProp and scored step by step with weighted tolerances, plus three-run variance; this is the closest single-domain analogue to EngTrace's code-derived milestones and repeated runs.

title: LPDS: Evaluating LLM Robustness Through Logic-Preserving Difficulty Scaling
notes: engineering_arxiv: must-cite - LPDS uses 100 EngTrace templates (with GSM-Symbolic and FinChain) to search for the hardest logic-preserving variations and reports that accuracy falls fastest on EngTrace variations; third-party use of EngTrace's templates that the revision should acknowledge and position against its paraphrase-robustness results.

title: Frontier-Eng: Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on Real-World Engineering Tasks with Generative Optimization
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - a 2026 engineering benchmark already cited by 11 papers (Semantic Scholar, 2026-10-01): 47 human-verified tasks in five engineering categories where agents iterate against industrial simulators and executable verifiers; it covers the tool-augmented, open-ended setting EngTrace leaves out and that the meta-review raised.

title: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - the newest large engineering-agent benchmark (1,301 expert-curated tasks, 26 professional software platforms, posted 29 Sep 2026) with programmatic verifiers that check final and intermediate artifacts; it marks the professional-software end of the spectrum EngTrace complements.

title: SoM-1K: A Thousand-Problem Benchmark Dataset for Strength of Materials
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - a static, expert-annotated mechanical benchmark of 1,065 strength-of-materials problems with diagrams (best model 56.6%), covering EngTrace's mechanical branch with real problems but no generated variants or step checks.

title: Large Language Models and their Awareness of Mechanics and Spatial Geometry
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - MecEng builds 84 multibody-simulation tasks from parameterized text descriptions and verifies the model each LLM produces (graph isomorphism, numerical solutions, mass, eigenfrequencies); a parameterized mechanical benchmark that checks the built artifact rather than the reasoning text.

title: CircuitSense: A Hierarchical MLLM Benchmark Bridging Visual Comprehension and Symbolic Reasoning in Engineering Design Process
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - 8,006+ synthetically generated circuit problems with auto-derived symbolic equation labels, showing symbolic derivation (below 19% for closed models) rather than perception is the bottleneck; the clearest generated-instance counterpart for EngTrace's electrical branch.

title: CircuChain: Disentangling Competence and Compliance in LLM Circuit Analysis
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - a circuit-analysis diagnostic of control/trap problem pairs whose symbolic-solver, SPICE and error-taxonomy pipeline attributes failures to convention, physics or arithmetic errors, documenting numerically correct answers that break the required method, the answer-versus-process gap EngTrace measures.

title: Evaluating LLM Reasoning in the Operations Research Domain with ORQA
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - the expert-built operations-research reasoning benchmark (ORQA, AAAI 2025) on multi-step optimization modeling, the natural reference for EngTrace's industrial branch.

title: OPT-Engine: Benchmarking the Limits of LLMs in Optimization Modeling via Complexity Scaling
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - an optimization-modeling benchmark with quantifiable, controllable complexity scaling across ten canonical OR problems (ICML 2026), reporting a robustness gap for pure chain-of-thought as complexity grows; a generated-instance design close to EngTrace's industrial templates.

title: StructureClaw: Traceable LLM Agents and an Executable Benchmark for Structural Engineering Workflows
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - an executable structural-engineering benchmark of 150 scenarios that requires one-to-one structural-model matching and numerical agreement with frozen solver references within a traceable artifact chain; the agentic counterpart to EngTrace's trace-level checks in the civil branch.

title: PE Civil Bench: Advancing Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation Performance of Large Language Models on Exam Problems and Automated Component Design
venue: Computer-Aided Civil and Infrastructure Engineering 2026, doi:10.1016/j.cacaie.2026.100126
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - a professional-exam benchmark of Fundamentals of Engineering and PE Civil questions (13 LLMs under plain prompting, RAG and agentic RAG) plus an agentic concrete-design pipeline with transparent traces; the licensure-exam reference point for EngTrace's civil branch (no arXiv version found; publisher PDF blocks scripted download).

title: CFDLLMBench: A Benchmark Suite for Evaluating Large Language Models in Computational Fluid Dynamics
venue: Journal of Data-Centric Machine Learning Research 2026 (arXiv 2509.20374)
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - a CFD benchmark suite (CFDQuery, CFDCodeBench, FoamBench) scored on code executability, solution accuracy and numerical convergence; with FEABench, which EngTrace already cites, it represents the simulation-agent line.

title: FEM-Bench: A Structured Scientific Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Code-Generating LLMs
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - a computational-mechanics benchmark of graduate-course finite-element coding tasks with objective verification, complementing FEABench on the simulation side and showing where mechanics reasoning is checked through code rather than text.

title: Capabilities of Large Language Models in Control Engineering: A Benchmark Study on GPT-4, Claude 3 Opus, and Gemini 1.0 Ultra
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - ControlBench, the widely cited undergraduate control-engineering benchmark judged by a panel of human experts for accuracy and reasoning (shares authors with TransportBench and EngDesign, both already cited); covers control within EngTrace's electrical branch.

title: TeleMath: A Benchmark for Large Language Models in Telecom Mathematical Problem Solving
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - 500 telecom problems with numerical answers, produced by a generation pipeline that expands expert-written seed problems; a communications-engineering analogue of EngTrace's seed-driven numeric problems.

title: EDU-CIRCUIT-HW: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models on Real-World University-Level STEM Student Handwritten Solutions
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - 1,300+ real student handwritten circuit solutions with expert-verified transcriptions and grading reports, showing that MLLM auto-grading of engineering work hides large latent recognition failures; an NLP-venue data point for EngTrace's judge-validity discussion.

title: Grading Handwritten Engineering Exams with Multimodal Large Language Models
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - an engineering-exam grading pipeline (ensemble of LLM graders, supervisor aggregation, deterministic validation) measured against lecturer grades on a held-out quiz, about 8 points mean absolute difference; evidence on how far LLM graders of engineering solutions can be trusted.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Homework Assessment in Circuit Analysis
venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education 35 (2025) (arXiv 2506.06390)
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - LLMs assess real student circuit-analysis solutions on completeness, method, final answer, arithmetic error and units, criteria that mirror EngTrace's checks; this group's FIE 2025 follow-up supplied the title that the May reference 'Liu et al., 2025' paired with the CIRCUIT arXiv id (see updates).

title: A$^{2}$utoLPBench: An Auto-Generated, Agent-Friendly LP Benchmark via Inverse-KKT Construction
notes: engineering_arxiv: should-cite - an LP benchmark that is a generator rather than a dataset: problems are built backwards from a chosen optimal primal-dual pair, so answers are correct by construction, difficulty is a knob and fresh seed ranges resist leakage; the same argument EngTrace makes for its private-seed templates, here for optimization in the industrial branch.

title: Can Large Language Models Solve Engineering Equations? A Systematic Comparison of Direct Prediction and Solver-Assisted Approaches
notes: engineering_arxiv: optional - 100 transcendental-equation problems from seven engineering domains solved by six frontier models directly versus with a Newton-Raphson solver (mean relative error cut by 67.9-81.8%); small, but direct evidence on the tool-augmented baselines the meta-review asked about.

title: EngIntervene: Benchmarking Multimodal Engineering State Understanding and Design Intervention Reasoning
notes: engineering_arxiv: optional - a multimodal benchmark of 3,229 questions in seven engineering domains organized into four levels (state grounding to design intervention), with levels 2-4 scored against structured references with atomic criteria; a very recent multi-domain suite to list beside EngVQA and ERI.

title: Can AI Master Construction Management (CM)? Benchmarking State-of-the-Art Large Language Models on CM Certification Exams
notes: engineering_arxiv: optional - CMExamSet, 689 multiple-choice questions from four accredited construction-management certification exams, analysed by subject, single- versus multi-step reasoning and figure use; a downloadable professional-certification benchmark to pair with PE Civil Bench.

title: CeProAgents: A Hierarchical Agents System for Automated Chemical Process Development
notes: engineering_arxiv: optional - introduces CeProBench, a six-task benchmark around knowledge, conceptual design and parameter simulation in chemical process development; the main arXiv evaluation found for EngTrace's chemical branch, though it is packaged with an agent system rather than released as a standalone benchmark.
